correctness.rationale: Central symmetry reduces the inradius to the reciprocal maximum Euclidean norm on the polar. Gauge-fixed incidence constraints form a bounded totally unimodular polytope, so strict convexity forces every maximizer to be an integer labeling. Complement of a maximum-degree-two graph has diameter two for n>=5. Level-zero/level-two sets force a deleted complete bipartite K_{a,b} with a,b<=2; the exact squared norm is a+b-(b-a)^2/n, and the 2-by-2 configuration exists precisely for a four-cycle component. Binary balanced patterns and the two feasible three-level patterns give the complete maximum and all tangent facets. Exact independent enumeration of 404 graph-component profiles through n=11 and arithmetic checks n=5..59 corroborates the proof; it is not used as an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The novelty is explicitly the sharp deterministic degree-two deletion formula, C4 obstruction, n=12/16 transition and complete tangent-facet count. Known graph-spread, polar and integer-labeling reductions are acknowledged. Full-text comparison of the strongest geometry and spread sources did not identify a statement logically covering these metric conclusions; the general facet theorem supplies ingredients rather than the optimized result.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact formula for graph spread of complements of degree-two graphs could cover the same Euclidean radius; searched sources do not establish its absence.
The self-complementary five-cycle is a small boundary instance; it does not dominate general complements of cycles at n>=6 or the four-cycle-threshold statements.
The general facet-vertex characterization is old, so novelty must not be attributed to integral Lipschitz optimization or the polarity identity.

value.rationale: Determines a natural complete family of exact Euclidean inradii and all tangent facet counts, with structural C4 obstruction, two sharp global dimension thresholds, radius stability under up to n sparse deletions and a contact-facet explosion at the n=16 boundary. These directly answer robustness of a geometric invariant under graph edge deletion, not a tiny gain or arbitrary finite recomputation.
